items.x_text:
APT29 watering holes: Sekoia links (moderate-to-high confidence) attacks on iOS 16.7, iOS 18.5 and Chrome for Android 139-145 to Midnight Blizzard. Visiting a compromised site was enough. Every flaw used was already patched: update.

#APT29 #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
No click. No download. Just opening a website. 📱

What BleepingComputer reported from Sekoia's research (4 Nov):
→ Compromised and lookalike sites in the U.S., Ukraine, the Czech Republic and Bulgaria profiled visitors' phones, then served a matching exploit chain with no user interaction
→ Targets: iOS 16.7, iOS 18.5 and Chrome for Android 139 to 145 (not 143)
→ On iOS 18.5 the payload harvested WhatsApp and Telegram data, Keychain credentials, location and photos
→ Sekoia attributes it to APT29 (Midnight Blizzard) with moderate-to-high confidence
→ Apple and Google had already patched every flaw used; nothing persisted after a reboot

What to do: update iOS and Chrome on every phone, push minimum OS versions through MDM, and treat old unsupported phones as untrusted for work data.

cover.hook: A French bank says attackers came in through a supplier. Reports say €118M moved.
cover.sub: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed the attack on 4 Nov. It won't confirm the figure, and says customers won't lose money.

slides.title: What the bank says
slides.body: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said on 4 Nov that attackers got in through "the platform of an external service provider", then made transfers to other financial institutions. Customer accounts were not used.

slides.label: reported loss ($133M), not confirmed by the bank

slides.title: Following the money
slides.body: Investigator ZachXBT raised his estimate of suspicious transactions above $133M. Bitquery traced about $108.8M in USDC withdrawals from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX on 1-2 Nov, but says it can't definitively link them to Arkéa.

slides.title: Where it stands
slides.body: The bank says it's contained, some funds are blocked and most suspended transfers resumed on 4 Nov. The Paris prosecutor has opened an investigation. The supplier and the attackers are not named.

slides.title: Do this week
items: List every supplier platform that can start a payment
Require out-of-band approval for large outbound transfers
Alert on unusual transfer volumes and new beneficiaries
Review vendor access to payment systems

items.question: Could a supplier's platform start a payment from your organisation without a second human check?

items.x_text:
OpenAI says an AI pipeline with an upcoming cyber model found and exploited 948 unique Linux local privilege escalation flaws for about $1.21M in API credits. All need local access first; 61 were patched upstream within 10 days.

#AISecurity #Linux
items.ig_caption:
948 Linux root exploits. Found by AI in one run. 🐧

What OpenAI's research shows (via Interesting Engineering, Unite.AI and AI Weekly, 4-5 Nov):
→ A prototype pipeline using an upcoming, unnamed OpenAI cyber model produced 948 unique working local privilege escalation exploits
→ It started from 2,308 candidate bugs; 1,724 were reproduced in isolated test VMs
→ Total cost: about $1.21M in API credits, roughly $1,279 per exploit
→ These need an attacker already on the machine: they turn a foothold into root
→ Ten days after the scan, 61 were patched upstream and 43 patches were staging; OpenAI says the goal is to help defenders fix bugs first

What to do: shorten your kernel patch cycle, plan for more kernel updates, and limit who gets a shell on your servers.

cover.hook: 1.09 million MUJI Card numbers may be exposed. With dates of birth.
cover.sub: MUJI operator Ryohin Keikaku confirmed it on 4 Nov. Names and CVV codes were not included, it says.

slides.title: Who's affected
slides.body: MUJI Card members who joined before July 2021. Exposed: credit card numbers and dates of birth. Ryohin Keikaku says cardholder names and CVV codes were not included.

slides.label: customers whose card data may be compromised
slides.note: Per Fuji News Network via Tokyo Reporter, 4-5 Nov 2026

slides.title: A second, smaller set
slides.body: Separately, 120 records with partial card numbers and names were exposed, from customers who registered payment details in the MUJI app or online store.

slides.title: Not the first this autumn
slides.body: In late October the company said a separate incident may have exposed up to 27.26 million email addresses and other profile data, with no financial data. It hasn't said how either breach happened.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Check card statements for small test charges
Ask your card issuer about a replacement card
Retailers: watch checkout for card-testing bursts

→ It affects MUJI Card members who joined before July 2021: card numbers and dates of birth

items.x_text:
Danish Meteorological Institute: names, emails, nationalities and pilot certificate numbers of about 5,000 pilots with Northavimet logins were downloaded. Access to the portal's user admin system began by 22 Oct. Pilots: change passwords.

#DataBreach #InfoSec
items.ig_caption:
5,000 pilots. Their details downloaded from a weather portal. ✈️

What The Copenhagen Post reported (Ritzau, 5 Nov):
→ The Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) says unauthorized people downloaded a list of about 5,000 pilots with Northavimet logins
→ Northavimet is a joint Nordic portal with weather for flight planning
→ Exposed: names, email addresses, nationalities and pilot certificate numbers
→ Intruders had access to a connected user admin system by 22 Oct; the portal was shut, updated and reopened
→ DMI reported it to police and the Danish data protection agency; how they got in hasn't been said

What to do: pilots should change their Northavimet password (and anywhere it's reused) and distrust emails that quote their certificate number.
